weekly_history.summary: Big moves in AI infrastructure and safety this week: the Model Context Protocol shipped its largest revision (stateless core, MRTR, RFC 9207 auth) and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 posted new coding/agentic SOTA, even as a Princeton/AISI/Stanford study showed frontier agents still fail at open-ended research judgment and a US push to restrict open-weight models gained steam. Physical sciences delivered: IBM/U Chicago claimed verifiable quantum advantage on logical circuits, Starship Flight 13 deployed the first Starlink V3 sats and survived reentry, LONGi hit a 35.5% tandem-cell record, and two gap sub-themes flipped active (iron-air storage via Ore Energy's 1 GWh deal; co-packaged optics via a silicon-photonics mass-production inflection). Bio saw an experiment-guided AlphaFold3 for structural ensembles, a CRISPR RNA-editing immuno-oncology result, and Moderna's mRNA-1010 flu vaccine heading to an Aug 5 FDA decision. New voice: Sayash Kapoor (Princeton, 'AI Snake Oil'); broad-scan adjacents surged in DAC, geothermal, and SMRs.

highlights.title: MCP ships 2026-07-28 spec: stateless core, MRTR, auth hardening
highlights.detail: The Model Context Protocol's biggest revision to date went live July 28, 2026, replacing the stateful session model with a stateless request/response core, adding Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing, cacheable list results, and RFC 9207 auth hardening; all Tier 1 SDKs (TS, Python, Go, C#) updated same day.

highlights.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 5, new SOTA on coding/agentic evals
highlights.detail: Released July 24, 2026, Opus 5 tops Frontier-Bench, CursorBench, ARC-AGI-3 and OSWorld 2.0 at roughly half Fable 5's cost, with a 1M-token context and 'xhigh' reasoning effort; Anthropic also reports it as its most aligned model to date.

highlights.title: Agility Robotics advances SPAC listing, opens Fremont Physical-AI hub
highlights.detail: Agility Robotics' merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI (pre-money ~$2.5B) is progressing toward a 2026 public listing; the company opened a 60,000 sq ft Fremont Physical AI hub, and Digit has logged 65,000+ operating hours across nine customer sites with $300M+ in multi-year orders.

highlights.detail: A new IIHS study (published July 23, 2026) comparing 50M driverless miles to 222B human miles across Phoenix, SF, LA and Austin found Waymo's crash-involvement rate 68% lower overall (85% lower for single-vehicle crashes, 81% lower for injury crashes), while flagging federal crash-reporting data is not yet adequate for monitoring large-scale AV expansion.

weekly_history.summary: Bio delivered the week's biggest move: Merck/Moderna's intismeran autogene became the first individualized mRNA cancer vaccine ever to win a Phase 3, hitting both RFS and DMFS in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma. On the AI side the story was post-training and harnesses rather than new base models — Z.ai's GLM-5.3 reused the GLM-5.2 base and moved Terminal-Bench 3.0 from 4.6% to 28.3% on post-training alone, while DeepSeek and Prime Intellect both open-sourced fully pluggable agent harnesses, and ACL/ICML award papers pinned down concrete failure modes in RLVR entropy control and diffusion-LM generation order. Hardware and energy saw real capital events: Etched at $21B with its first rack delivered to Jane Street, Form Energy's $750M Series G against an 80 GWh iron-air backlog, and General Fusion becoming the first publicly traded fusion developer. Verification was unusually harsh this week — eight items were dropped, including three for out-of-window dates that had been dressed up as current, one duplicate of last week's merge, and four that no resolving source could confirm before the session's search budget ran out.

weekly_history.summary: Hot Chips 2026 (Aug 23-25) dominated the week: Nvidia detailed Rubin/Vera, AMD detailed MI400/MI455X and the Helios rack, and OpenAI publicly unveiled Jalapeno, its first Broadcom-built custom inference ASIC. Two long-standing hardware gap sub-themes finally got real items from the same venue - photonic/optical compute (Opticore's homodyne tensor crossbar) and consumer/edge NPUs (UC Berkeley's Gemmelos). In bio, FDA approved Mounjaro for cardiovascular risk reduction, Moderna/Merck posted the first-ever positive Phase 3 for an individualized mRNA cancer vaccine, and Charite published a six-patient CAR-T reversal of refractory rheumatoid arthritis in Nature Medicine. The week's dominant thesis across voices was that the AI build-out's binding constraint has moved from chip supply to power, skilled labor, and capital. Verification: 29 passed, 5 fixed (a fabricated 16% all-cause-mortality figure on Mounjaro, a wrong Starship Flight 14 date, a stale Dwarkesh URL, a backfill flag), 0 dropped. Entity reconciliation added 7 players we were tracking the news about but not the player behind it - Opticore, Charite Berlin, BindCraft/EPFL, Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, Inherent, Inertia Enterprises, and Quantum Circuits Inc (the Yale spinout whose dual-rail qubit D-Wave's Nature result actually rests on).

meta.title: Ceiling / Bets — B / 10B / T value-creation tiers
meta.refresh: monthly (big-ideas-ceiling-refresh task) + re-rendered every weekly dashboard build

scale.T: Trillion-scale: could anchor a $1T+ company or reshape a multi-trillion slice of the economy.
scale.10B: Tens of billions: could mint $10B–$100B+ companies / category-defining markets.
scale.B: Single-digit billions: real, valuable $1–10B outcomes — important but more contained or diffuse.

rubric: Value capture & defensibility (IP, scale, data, network, regulatory moat)
meta.note: Category tier = the ceiling of the category's biggest plausible winner; bet tier = that specific player's realistic ceiling. That's why every category is 10B/T (they're all 'big ideas') while individual bets span B/10B/T — most companies, even in a trillion-dollar arena, top out at B/10B.
meta.disclaimer: Forward-looking, opinionated analysis for prioritization — NOT investment advice. Tiers are speculative upper bounds (what's possible if the bet works), not predictions or valuations. Do your own diligence.

categories.name: Transformers / LLMs / coding agents
categories.tam_note: Frontier models + the coding-agent layer sit on top of nearly all knowledge work.
categories.capture: Concentrated: a few labs + whoever owns the agent/IDE layer; open weights compress margins.
categories.rationale: The clearest 'next-OpenAI' arena — a single frontier lab or winning agent layer can reach trillion-scale, and the revenue has caught up to the valuations: Anthropic reported ~$11.5B of Q2 2026 revenue against OpenAI's ~$6.7B (its first quarter ahead) on a ~$65B run-rate exiting July, and on Sep 1 shipped Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 with a gated capability tier (Mythos restricted to US cyber and life-sciences verification programs) ahead of an October listing that Bloomberg/Fortune report is being pitched at ~$2T — FLAG: reported target, last confirmed primary mark is the ~$965B Series H-1. OpenAI's CFO now says 'public company in 2027'. Open weights keep compressing the price floor (Qwen3.8-Max at ~1/4 GPT-5.6 pricing; GLM-5.3 gaining on post-training alone), but the layer above the models is consolidating: SpaceX bought Cursor for $60B and NVIDIA agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.93B (Sep 3).

categories.name: RLHF + reasoning models (test-time compute)
categories.tam_note: Reasoning is a capability multiplier on the same frontier-lab franchises.
categories.capture: Accrues to the #01 frontier labs; the method (RLVR) itself is diffuse/replicable.
categories.rationale: Verifiable rewards are turning into real scientific output: OpenAI's internal Astra published Lean-4-verified solutions to ten decade-plus-open math/CS problems for ~$2,000 of inference compute (Aug 1, 2026), with machine-checkable certificates — the strongest evidence yet that reasoning models generate value rather than just benchmark scores. Small challengers are also landing punches (Inherent's 27B Faraday agent claims to beat frontier models at reproducing published research), but the value still accrues to the same trillion-scale labs rather than a separate company. New this month: the frontier is now being released behind capability gates — OpenAI began a phased rollout of GPT-6 Astra on Sep 3 as the first model to hit its internal 'Critical' cyber threshold (access first via the Daybreak program), and Anthropic's Mythos 5.1 is restricted to verified cyber/life-sciences programs. Gating shifts value toward the labs that can clear regulators, and away from open replication.

Every model winner still pays this layer — and the capital is now piling into the neocloud/datacenter tier just above it: Crusoe raised $3B at $30B (Atreides/Valor, Sep 2026, ~3x in under a year) and Fluidstack $1.5B at $18B (Jane Street) in the same week. categories.capture: Duopoly (Lilly, Novo) with oral + next-gen widening; strong IP + manufacturing moats.

The duopoly also got messier: Novo's CagriSema missed HbA1c non-inferiority vs tirzepatide, while Novo's oral semaglutide outsold Lilly's Foundayo roughly 5-to-1 in the first head-to-head quarter (~$496M vs $98M).

categories.capture: Spread across several editors; each drug is 10B-scale, not a single trillion-dollar firm.
categories.rationale: In vivo editing keeps inflecting clinically (Intellia's lonvo-z pivotal Phase 3 in HAE; VERVE-102 base editing at PCSK9 −88% / LDL-C −62%; Prime's first in vivo prime-editing trial), and Casgevy is finally showing a commercial ramp at $76M in Q2 2026 (+151% YoY). The counterweight is that bespoke, per-patient editing looks economically brutal: Doudna and Urnov's Aurora Therapeutics abandoned its lead PKU program and cut staff seven months in (Aug 5, 2026), outpaced by Beam's off-the-shelf base editor. Durable franchises, not one giant.

categories.name: Quantum error correction / FT quantum
categories.tam_note: Fault-tolerant quantum could crack materials, chemistry, and crypto.
categories.capture: Long-dated; value likely captured by cloud parents (Google/IBM/AWS) + a few pure-plays.
categories.rationale: Logical-qubit counts are now a real scoreboard rather than a single-digit demo: as of August 2026 five organizations have demonstrated verified logical qubits, led by QuEra (96 logical from 448 physical) and Quantinuum (48 logical from 98 physical on Helios, ~99.921% two-qubit fidelity and near-five-nines logical fidelity, heading to Oracle Cloud). Consolidation is also underway — IBM buying HRL for silicon-spin qubits, D-Wave buying Quantum Circuits for $550M. Genuinely useful FT machines are still years out; 10B base case, T-upside on a long fuse.

wildcards.name: Firm power for AI datacenters (EGS + SMRs)
wildcards.why: PROMOTED 10B→T. The dominant thesis across tracked voices this month is that the AI build-out's binding constraint has moved from chip supply to power — and firm, clean, sited-anywhere generation is now a financeable business, not a demo. Fervo IPO'd on Nasdaq (FRVO) in May 2026 at $27/share on an upsized 70M-share offering, has a 3 GW framework with Google, and expects Cape Station's first 100 MW on the grid in October 2026; Valar Atomics raised $1B (Sequoia-led, ~$6B) for factory-built SMRs already powering an Nvidia Blackwell cluster. The buyers are now financed at scale too — Crusoe (an AI-datacenter builder and Form Energy customer) raised $3B at $30B and Fluidstack $1.5B at $18B in the first week of September. Whoever supplies datacenter-grade firm power is selling into a trillion-scale capex cycle.

Add Inherent's Faraday agent reproducing published findings, plus autonomous-lab startups (Periodic ~$300M seed, Lila $200M). If models reliably generate verified discoveries, value compounds across every R&D-driven industry.

wildcards.why: Autonomous cyber agents went operational — GPT-5.6 Sol chained a zero-day and stolen creds to breach Hugging Face's production infra (Jul 2026), triggering a bipartisan AI 'Kill Switch' bill — and the defense market is repricing fast: Horizon3 raised $250M at a $2B valuation (Aug 2026) on 310,000 autonomous pentests run, alongside XBOW ($120M Series C at $1B+) and Wiz's first agentic supply-chain incident write-ups. Large security TAM plus a genuinely new dual-use risk surface.
